steps.what: Determine system requirements and safe test conditions
Write and configure the robot or vision program
Run repeated specified sandbox tests and collect their outputs
Interpret test results and perform physical validation under site procedures
Record findings and check the exact deployment package and target
Deploy the authorised package to the specified robot controller

tasks.design: Use native project skeletons in the robot programming and simulation environment represented by {OTHER}, then batch only specified sandbox tests. Keep algorithm design, interpretation, physical validation and the final deployment decision human, with a gate on the exact controller package rather than on ordinary author saves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated program scaffolding and sandbox test launches take manual interaction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project templates and deterministic test runners.
tasks.still_hard: Vision generalisation, device integration and demonstrating acceptable physical behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Identify failure modes that a passing synthetic test does not reveal.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated setup and test interaction; engineering authority unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: robot development environments can reuse project scaffolding and repeat specified sandbox tests, without replacing physical validation.

assumptions: Provisional shares count technician labour, not robot execution or simulation runtime. The scenario includes actual deployment by an already authorised technician.

s1 produces interfaces, versions, camera calibration references, test inputs and expected outcomes; missing calibration or requirements require manual work. s2 creates the exact candidate tested in s3. No ready-labelled image corpus is assumed; any actual capture or labelling must be added to s1 before estimating.
Test native templates and test runners first. Only standard scaffolding loses 2.5 points in s2, not vision algorithm design. s3 removes repeated manual launches and output collection only.

s5 includes the actual validation record and complete deployment package check after physical validation. A changed program must return through tests and validation; it cannot reuse approval. Ordinary author saves remain fully retained.
If a separate commissioning authority is required, count that actual role's approval before deployment rather than inventing technician authority.
unknowns: Required image capture and labelling effort
research_questions: How much manual sandbox interaction remains after excluding existing unattended runs?

incremental.description: Maintain scaffolding and deterministic sandbox fixtures

approvals.approved_version: s5 exact tested program version, dependencies and controller target; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 2.5 scaffold points plus 15 repeated sandbox-interaction points=17.5; less 1.5 upkeep gives 16. With a new vision interface, retain custom code and novel tests: only 0.5 scaffold point and 4 compatible fixture-run points disappear, leaving 3 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop efficient and safe robotic path motions

steps.what: Observe the cell and verify workpiece, tooling and clearance constraints
Design candidate motions and specify simulation comparisons
Repeat specified simulation runs and assemble comparison outputs
Interpret outputs and validate physical path behaviour under site procedures
Record path findings and authorise the exact controller motion package
Load the authorised motion package to the specified controller

tasks.design: Use the native batch-run facility of the robot simulation environment in {OTHER} for technician-specified candidate motions. Keep path design and real-cell validation human, preserve the separate {DOCS} validation record, and gate only the actual controller load on its final validated version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual repetition of comparison runs and output collection.
tasks.enabler_now: Native simulation batching without autonomous path selection.
tasks.still_hard: Model fidelity, changing tooling and trade-offs among speed, safety and quality.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise clearance or process effects missing from the digital cell model.
tasks.altitude: Less simulator interaction, with path responsibility unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: batch simulation can repeat specified robot-motion comparisons but does not establish physical safety.

assumptions: Provisional focal shares exclude all existing simulation and robot runtime. This is a path-specific task instance, not the same programming work counted a second time in a roll-up.

Cell engineering supplies model geometry and tool versions; s1 checks physical correspondence and captures missing constraints. s2 supplies candidate identifiers, loads, speeds and comparison measures. Incompatible geometry requires manual repair before s3.
Native batching is tested first. Only repeated manual simulation interaction disappears; path design, interpretation, physical validation, factual record writing and ordinary saves remain.
s5 approves an actual controller load after final validation, not an author save. Changed motions or targets void approval. A separate commissioning sign-off, if real, must be counted before s6.
unknowns: Whether comparison runs already execute unattended
research_questions: Which comparison launches and output placements are still manual?

incremental.description: Maintain comparison-run specifications and model-version checks

approvals.approved_version: s5 exact validated motion version and controller target; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15 repeated-interaction points less 1 upkeep gives 14. With changed tooling and unreliable clearance geometry, retain model repair and most comparisons; only 3 points of compatible cycle-output runs replay, giving 2 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train robots through software and interactive tests

steps.what: Specify the task and capture training examples and test conditions
Interactively teach behaviours and configure training software
Repeat specified offline tests and collect training outputs
Evaluate generalisation and validate actual task behaviour
Record findings and authorise the final trained behaviour package
Load the exact authorised trained package onto its target robot

tasks.design: Batch fixed offline test repetitions in the robot-training environment represented by {OTHER}, after the technician creates actual examples and the test specification. Keep interactive teaching and real behaviour validation human, with a separate recorded final-package check before its controller load.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technicians can manually launch repeated offline checks and collect their outputs.
tasks.enabler_now: Native offline test batching, without automating physical experiments or inventing training examples.
tasks.still_hard: Generalisation, experiment-specific constraints and detecting unsafe learned behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: See when task success masks an unacceptable physical or scientific outcome.
tasks.altitude: Less test-launch repetition, with teaching and acceptance decisions unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed offline test batching can reduce launch interactions while interactive robot teaching and physical validation remain human.

assumptions: Shares are provisional technician labour; existing training-software runtime and robot execution earn no saving. This task is training an actual behaviour, not duplicating a separately counted software deployment instance.

s1 includes manual example capture and supplies task identifier, example provenance and test conditions. s2 supplies exact candidate version, repeat inputs and expected measures. Missing examples require actual capture; no synthetic success labels.
Test native offline batching first. s3 removes manual launches/output gathering only, not test design, chemical handling, physical robot repetitions or scientific result interpretation.

s5 includes the actual training record and complete package/target decision. Ordinary author saves are fully retained; s6 is a distinct controller load whose approval is void after changes. Add any actual commissioning authority before loading.
unknowns: Actual example capture and labelling workload
research_questions: Separate offline launch interaction from all physical experiments and existing training runtime.

incremental.description: Maintain offline test fixtures and example-version correspondence

approvals.approved_version: s5 exact validated trained package, dependencies and robot target; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15 repeated offline-interaction points less 1.5 upkeep gives 13.5. A new chemical-sample protocol needs fresh examples and novel physical checks; only 4 points of compatible offline repetitions can be batched, leaving 2.5 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Count and identify actual sensors, cables and other supplies
Enter observed item quantities and locations into the stock record
Compare entered observations against expected quantities and stock limits
Investigate discrepancies and determine actual stock corrections
Record verified corrections and save the inventory record

tasks.design: Configure location defaults and item lookup in the maintenance-stores module of {OPS_SYSTEM}, retaining actual counting and quantity capture. Run exact quantity and stock-limit comparisons separately, leaving discrepancy investigation and the ordinary correction save human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual location-reference entry and line-by-line comparisons.
tasks.enabler_now: Native stock-count forms and exact variance views.
tasks.still_hard: Unlabelled cables, compatible substitutes and unrecorded removals.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what a physical item really is and explain why the stock record differs.
tasks.altitude: Less comparison work, with stock responsibility unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: stock forms and exact variance views can reduce repeated reference entry and comparison, without counting items or resolving discrepancies.

assumptions: Provisional shares cover actual inventory maintenance, not purchasing or supplier orders. The stock correction is the author's ordinary same-system record write, fully retained and ungated.

s1 produces item identification, location, unit and actual quantity; s2 manually enters or scans these facts. The stores process supplies item master, recorded transactions and approved stock limits. Missing identifiers or unrecorded movements go to s4, not automatic reconciliation.

Test native forms and variance views first. Only repeated location references lose two points in s2. s3 removes an actual manual comparison; if the current view already compares automatically, remove that baseline. Existing system runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Quality of item labels and unit definitions
research_questions: Observe one real count and identify remaining manual comparison work.

incremental.description: Maintain stock-location defaults and exact comparison mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 2 reference-entry points plus 15 comparison points=17, less 0.7 upkeep gives 16.3. With mixed unlabelled parts and inconsistent units, only 0.5 reference-entry point and 3 exact-match comparison points disappear; identification and discrepancies stay human, leaving 2.8 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
